info.title: Upgrading to &sle; with the distribution migration system

abstract.para: This section describes the actual upgrade procedure with the distribution migration system.

listitem.para: The cluster services must be stopped on all nodes. Run crm cluster status to make sure both &pace; and &corosync; are inactive.
The system must be registered with the &scc; or an &rmt; server. "Pay as you go" instances in the public cloud are automatically registered to the SUSE-operated update infrastructure.
The upgrade path must be supported. Refer to for details.
The upgrade target is set to &productnumber; instead of the default 16.0. Refer to for details.

The server that provides the migration target must have the appropriate repositories synced, and they must be up to date. This requirement is automatically met by the &scc;, and the &suse;-operated update infrastructure in the public cloud. If you are using an &rmt; server, make sure to mirror all relevant channels.

The operating system needs to reside on a single partition. Support for multiple partitions, such as LVM, is limited to configurations where the separated partitions do not contain OS-critical data or processes. For example, a separate /home partition will function whereas a separate /var will not.

section.title: Upgrading &productname; 15 to &productnumber;
section.para: The distribution migration system can be invoked using two different methods:

listitem.para: Reboot after installing the suse-migration-sle16-activation package.
Run the run_migration command included with the SLES16-Migration package.

section.para: Depending on your architecture, perform the following steps to trigger the upgrade:

listitem.para: After installing the suse-migration-sle16-activation package, start the migration process by rebooting the system:
The suse-migration-sle16-activation package installs SLES16-Migration as a dependency and modifies the bootloader configuration to boot into the upgrade image.
Modifying the boot loader configuration is not supported on &s390x;, so you start the migration directly with run_migration.
The run_migration utility uses &kexec; and does not work in &xen;-based environments. If &kexec; causes a kernel panic, refer to the TID at and set the soft_reboot customization option (see ).

section.para: After the upgrade, the &ha; cluster services will start automatically during system boot (if the &pace; service is enabled). The cluster resources will start again when the upgraded cluster stack is back online and reaches a quorate state.
